name: WooCommerce
description: Ecommerce: open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin with a REST API for products, orders, customers, coupons and more on self-hosted stores.
access_notes: WooCommerce is a free open-source WordPress plugin. Store admins generate consumer key/secret pairs at WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API on their own site. Over HTTPS the key/secret are used via HTTP Basic Auth (or query params); over plain HTTP, OAuth 1.0a one-legged HMAC-SHA1 signatures are required. Access to a third-party merchant's store requires that store's admin to issue keys.
mcp_notes: Official WooCommerce MCP integration ships in WooCommerce core (developer preview/beta since 10.3): enable in Settings > Advanced > Features, connect via @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote proxy to /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp authenticated with REST API keys. No Composio WooCommerce toolkit found (composio.dev/toolkits/woocommerce and docs.composio.dev/toolkits/woocommerce both return 404).
uncertainty_notes: The API is per-store (self-hosted WordPress), so there is no central developer portal; integrating with someone else's store requires their admin to generate keys. Vendor MCP is still labeled developer preview/beta.

evidence.note: Official auth docs: HTTP Basic Auth with consumer key/secret over HTTPS; OAuth 1.0a one-legged HMAC signature for non-SSL.
Merchant-facing doc: generate REST API keys self-serve at WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API with read/write permission levels.
Full REST reference: CRUD for orders, products, customers, coupons, plus a /webhooks endpoint and HMAC-SHA256-signed webhook deliveries.
Official docs: native MCP support in WooCommerce core via WordPress MCP Adapter and @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote proxy, authenticated with REST API keys.
WooCommerce developer blog: MCP integration beta announced in WooCommerce 10.3.
